Amazing. Easily one of the best games ever made. Graphics are OUTSTANDING so is game play. It also runs very very well with no stuttering or issues which is super rare in today's day and age (looking at you Borderlands 4).

I refuse to buy games that run like hot garbage... Jedi Survivor, BL4, the new Monster Hunter... they all look like great games but the performance is so dog water, I don't want to support devs like that so I refuse to spend money on them until they are fixed. This game runs AMAZING and looks amazing. BUY BUY BUY.

Horrible performance (constant audio cut-offs and fps stutters in cutscenes + generally unstable overall), Boring Story, Enemies beeing way too aggressive that you can't even get up at times, "Puzzles" beeing too lengthy and annoying.

And if you wanna complete 100% of the games achievements, you have to play the entire game again (including Sidequests)

Continuation of Zero Dawn. More of the same, for better or worse. Fans of the first would enjoy the sequel.

i liked the dlc more than the main story :P new game+ items through tokens are stoopid. these tokens are obtained through completing main quest, side quests, and more. it takes a long time to obtain enough tokens to buy all new game+ items to obtain the achievement. other than that, 8/10

Great port. Played it on PS5 but not the DLC, so replaying the whole thing here at higher fps and settings. Running on a 4080 and using dynamic res scaling to lock fps ~90. Runs like a dream.

For people with 8GB of vram or less trying to run at 4k: check out digital foundries' optimized settings video. Also if on nvidia, check out upgrading the DLSS used by the game, newer version consumes less vram.

Incredible experience.
The atmosphere and the graphics are breathtaking.
Combat is greatly improved and is such a nice addition with the different machines and NPCs
A great game all around and a must play (after Zero Dawn of course).
Visually stunning, cant complain... Dont overclock GPU or RAM (xmp) can lead to repeated crashing. it happened to me at first then turning the overclock off fixed it

Great game. Got it working on steam deck after googling the settings for it. Been playing for over 400 hours and the game hasn't froze up. Still some of the missions are just repetitive like Zero Dawn.

Significant downgrade from the first game. Buggy enemy interactions. Scanning takes longer and has to be re applied every 5 seconds. Basic enemies will randomly 1 shot you from full health. Any interaction prompt, including silent strike, is likely to only appear in one pixel perfect location resulting in having to walk around back and forth just to get the prompt to show up. Getting hit once results in being locked into a 30 second standing up animation. Every enemy rapidly wriggles and writhes to ensure their weak spots only stay in one place for a few milliseconds at a time and hits anywhere other than weak spots do single digit damage.

I have a great memory playing the first Horizon. I just finished university and didn't know what to do next. Killing machines and bad guys with bows and arrows filled that time. 

Forbidden West is more of that. Beautiful game with smooth combat. 

My only issue is the occasional graphic glitches but tweaking the settings have helped.

This game is great, after playing Hogwarts Legacy which I loved, I was looking for a fun game that wasn't too dark. This game isn't depressing or too gory like Baldur's Gate3 which got too dark for me.

2nd playthrough on easiest setting and I'm still 223 hours in, not even completing all the collectables. This is a massive game with a wide variety of play. From fighting to environmental puzzles to earning the ability to turn enemies on your side with "cauldrons", and more this games has kept me having fun and has felt fresh the whole way through.
One of my all-time favourite games, second only to HZD. Plays well on PC, graphics hold up. Gameplay is great. Story is brilliant.

If you liked the first game, definitely buy this. The character models are significantly improved, visuals are overall much better. The combat is a bit more involved and will take time getting used to but not a problem. Lots of amazing side quests as well.
So blown away by this game and this series. What an incredible world we get to experience. Can't recommend it more.

Epitome of a gold standard sequel. Literally the first game but with better everything.

I’m all for a firey red headed female protagonist who tears down giant machine monsters. Hopefully they don’t make her too woke in a sequel to this sequel

It has a lot of elements of the first while also still having a unique story. I was worried it would have "second game" syndrome, but it's fairly solid. The game play has some things I don't like, such as the random ways conversations are just entire cut scenes and you can't just go through the dialogue faster by reading, but the new machines and world building is really interesting. I enjoy the Tenakth people especially and their discord with the Carja. Lots to love this this sequel.

If you've played Horizon Zero Dawn and liked it, you will love Forbidden West. It has more and better of the same--better graphics, better facial animations (so lifelike!), better climbing mechanics, better stealth, better combat, better weapons, MORE ROCKS, and the laundry list goes on. Aloy is a little annoying at times than in HZD, though, but the story is also bigger in every way.

This is an incredible and very well-implemented port, with amazing performance. I never experienced any FPS drops even in wide areas with enemies, particles, and details.

The graphics and art of this game are incredibly beautiful. I loved seeing every landscape, every detail in the environment (for example, the snow, moving leaves). Every single detail immerses you deeply into the game.
The combat in the game is a lot of fun. You must alternate between ranged and melee combat depending on your enemy. The available combos and abilities add a great variety to the combat style.
Without going into too much detail, I highly recommend trying out this game.

compared to the first, this one is clunky, the UI is worse, the gameplay is worse, the skillsets are worse. Everything is badder and the story must be on a slow burn because I'm bored.

Loved the first one. Can't be bothered grinding through this one to find out what happens. Yuck.

Years later - played through HZD again. Such a great game. Tried so hard to get through this. Can't. Its uniquely terrible gameplay is just too frustrating to tolerate and the story is mediocre and doesn't compel tolerance of this nonsense.

A beautiful game with excellent animations, troubled by a mountain of oversights.
They made a game with heavy emphasis on both melee and bow combat, but made melee almost completely worthless. 10+ melee combos that you have to spend skill points to unlock, and that don't serve a purpose in actual combat or deal meaningful damage.
Half of the attacks performed by machines feel unnecessarily punishing, with many of them having lingering hitboxes that make them impossible to dodge reliably.
Introduced a few different mechanics that require main story progression to unlock, punishing people that try to do side missions first.
Some of the puzzles are at the level where a toddler would find them easy, and some you can't figure out until you accrue 10 minutes of Aloy's verbal hints. Even then, the puzzles are buggy and clearly untested, as they don't always function properly even when you have the correct answer.
Many of the puzzles and obstacles can be just jumped around in ways that clearly weren't intended to benefit veteran players.
It gets harder to convince yourself to keep playing the farther in you get, which is partially because the writing gets worse as you play. Like with every side quest, they wrote themselves into a corner before they even started writing. It's bizarre.
I just wouldn't recommend this unless you're going to play on a low difficulty, and skip half the side missions and all of the optional collectibles. The frustration isn't worth it.
Another awesome game from PlayStation! The story was so good. The Burning Shores story was pretty good too. The graphics are beautiful.
Very good sequel to Horizon Zero Dawn. Maybe a bit too much stuff going on, but you can ignore a lot as well.
The game was OK but I enjoyed the 1st game a lot more. I wish companies would stop franchising games. If they will make a 3rd one I would not buy it.
It amazes me how massive this open world map is, and how many side quests are available that help strengthen, rather than distract from, the main quest.
Fun follow up to Zero Dawn. Looks gorgeous and plays well. Only thing I don’t like is that, compared to ZD, it kinda has too much to do. But to be clear, it’s not a huge issue.

Dual sense controller some how locked my game at 15 fps.
After I changed it to an xbox controller the lag was was fixed.
Smooth 120fps on 2k reso

Great follow-up to Horizon: Zero Dawn, absolutely can't wait for the finale. If you liked the first one, you'll like this one, if you haven't played either, then start with Zero Dawn. Game play is fast paced during combat, and slower during exploration, although it speeds up steadily as you progress and gain new abilities/options. Don't invest all your time into the Arena if you're in it for the weapons, Burning Shores has by far the best gear in the game, and its pretty easily attainable, especially comparatively.
the first game was amazing and this one builds on that and is equally as good. Have not beat the game yet but so far i am really enjoying the story and gameplay.

Forbidden west on pc really shines with its amazing graphics and very impressive performance (runs above 100 fps with no upscaling, highest settings, on my 4090).
You can really get more frames out of this game when adjusting the settings right to you rig.

Story wise I cant tell anything about it, because i only played through the first couple of scenes. But the opening sequences do make a good impression.

The Price of 60€ is more than pleasant, because you get the complete edition with the burning shores dlc.

Deffinitly recommended.

This game is a piece of crap. It was very clearly not tested on the higher difficulties because you will spend more time looking at the insufferable load screen than playing the actual game

Idiot developers, I know you wont read this. But upping the damage on everything so it one shots the player character is not good game design. That does not make your game challenging. That makes your game punishing.

And good job locking the difficulty too. So If I want to unfuck your terrible design choices I have to start from scratch.

Sure I can play perfectly and dodge all the crap the game throws my way. or maybe ill get unlucky and the ai will do something completely unexpected and .. guess what... one shot.

And who was the genius who thought it was a good idea to make a hunting ground challenge around shocking robots and hitting them with arena traps?

Jumping robots and very very small arena traps.

Terrible. It feels like I got into a time machine and played one of ubisofts tired ass open world games.
I am sure there is an award winning story or something 

But I am to damn distracted by this awful game play.
Might be my first time ever after i finish a game to start a NewGame+. Love this title, everything about the game is just amazing. The story line is everything you need. Can't wait for the next one!

A very beautiful and immersive game. It has an amazing store line and continuation from the first game pretty much like you just left off almost. Obviously you have to relocate all of your weapons/amour/upgrades but all in all, its an amazing game the graphics are out of this world.

Great base game, great mechanics, great setting. The DLC contains one of the worst written, Mary Sue romantic interests in the history of gaming who you cannot even turn down (so much for consent) and who you WILL fall in love for because she is SO AMAZING. Not due to her actions, but because Aloy will TELL YOU CONSTANTLY. She is JUST THE BEST. Personality of cardboard, angsty and devoid of any positive traits such as humility or self-awareness, no character arc or progression, but she IS the best person in the ENTIRE GAME.

It is the gold star example of the heights of bad writing that came out of the industry during the "Gamer Gate" period; this is coming from an opponent of the "anti woke" brigade who is more than comfortable with LGBT relationships. Being LGBT isn't a personality and it isn't a character trait, nor does it make you immediately attractive.

Play it, learn to fast skip all the DLC dialogues with its main character (which certainly is not Aloy).

Review added because I'm coming back to finish the NG+ years after 100% (all achievements) the game and I still remember the DLC with a bad taste in my mouth even before installing it.

The Horizon series is quickly becoming my all-time favorite series in gaming, and Forbidden West is the reason for it. The story is fantastic (though not quite as groundbreaking as that of Zero Dawn), the gameplay has vastly improved from the first game, the world is absolutely massive, and the graphics and animation is plain old stunning. As far as open-world western-style RPGs go, this game has it all: stealth ranged combat, monster hunting, fantastic voice acting and mocap, and a gorgeous environment.

Perhaps the only quarrel I have with the game is in its melee combat, which—though much better than the first game's—still feels a bit wonky.

If you're interested in a beautiful, AAA, action RPG with a massive open world and an excellent story, definitely give Horizon Forbidden West a look.

Incredible masterpiece of a game despite being under the frustrating and annoying weight of a grind slog to update your weapons, gear, and skills. For completionists, unless your willing to relax and spend a few hundred hours, this will be infuriating. 

Like Zero Dawn, the combat is top notch and incredibly exciting at times. It too is annoyingly weighted down by stamina management, weapon loading, and other completely unnecessary obstacles. Actually, there is almost too much too manage. A simplified combat experience would have been more enjoyable. But still, nothing quite like taking down a big machine or doing melee combat with several machines at once.

They've smoothed out some of the buggy eye movement of Zero Dawn quite well as cut scenes look and feel quite natural now. Side missions are actually quite well voice acted and written so you find yourself in no hurry to complete the main quest. There is a ton of content for you to engage in at your leisure.

All in all, a fantastic game...if you can get by the grind slog.

While I do recommend this game, it's not better than the original. This one suffers from over inflation. I'm 73hrs in, I haven't finished the main story line, and I have no idea how close to the end I am. There are also large sections of the map I've barely touched.

Some parts of the story are really good. Others parts feel like they were crammed in. 

The reason you get at the start about why you've lost all your weapons and powers, is just dumb.

The overhaul of the climbing system is a big step back. 

The world is varied and stunning. Despite it's massive size, no corner of the map feels recycled. 

If you liked the first one, you'll enjoy this one, but it might burn you out. It's just so big...

What's with all the lesbians? Seriously, why does Alloys sexuality even matter when shes trying to save the world. Couldn't they had just left it as an awesome game about fighting mechanical dinos? Some of my best friends in real life are gay, but I don't need one in every video game I pick up. Being straight or gay adds nothing to the game. It's pathetic virtue signaling.
The first game is an absolute masterpiece and this sequel is panning out so far to be even better! Incredible game, worth every cent.
Good game play, a bit confusing but overall pretty good - not perfect performance port wise but playable and decent. Pick up on a sale for sure
one of the greatest storys and gameplay ive ever played. coming form someone with 700 hours on monster hunter world
Excellent game! A strong sequel with everything I loved from the first game and a little more added on top to keep things fresh.

The story is amazing, but the controls are absolutely terribly designed. Double tap to dodge by default? On a PC? Every time I tried to move slowly on a cliff I just dove right off. The platforming is also terrible, half the time Aloy jumps the wrong way. Using the space button to activate pull to spot and hold to shieldwing? Why does the button do multiple things???? And the damn V button. Can't scan anything if there's a stupid vision point around. The devs of this game should be ashamed. I want to love this game so much, but the stupid points of failure are just too game breaking.

A few graphic bugs, you have to sort it out in the settings depends on graphics card. Highly recommend playing with PS4 controller so you can use motion controllers. Almost identical to PS game, slightly less details at max though.
Fantastic game ! A few teeny glitches here and there during combat or when you follow an npc, but pretty rare, runs great otherwise. Highly recommended if you liked the first one !

There have been a lot of comment on how irritating Aloy become in this game, the skill tree does not make any sense, the weapons and the upgrades just went overboard without any sensible concept with the tons of crafting material added to the game.
It seems to be developers should also learn some common sense and not try to fix which is not broken.

Nevertheless I still enjoyed the game for more than 60 hours with only 3 crashes. However after the last patch the game become completely unplayable as crashes on launch or after maximum 1-2 minutes play.

It may will be better later, but for now it feels as I am used as beta tester while paying the full price for the game.

I have much to say about it honestly, but I have to cut it short (sadly).
I decided to buy and play Horizen Forbidden West, because I really really liked Horizen Zero Dawn. It was one of the best single-player games I've ever played, and now Horizen Forbidden West joins with it.
It had its highs and lows, but the highs dominated. One big low was the climbing (only sometimes) when Aloy doesn't realize, that she is suppose to go my way and there is nothing what could possibly block that way but she still can do it, frustrating. But it wasn't too often.
The highest high is obviously the story. Sony did a remarkably good job when creating the storyline and not just in the main story and the DLC is also a banger of content (I can only recommend it and its a free 4h+ storyline add-on).
What can I say now. Actually, nothing. I loved playing it and I'm really looking forward to play the third part and I pray it won't take too long for Sony to deliver that banger.
If you're thinking about buying this game, I can ensure you, you are doing nothing wrong. Just do it and broaden your Horizon.
